What you are asked to decide

Choice 1 and choice 3

Systems maps: the studio's pick

Loop Lines draws the whole system as a transit map on Prussian. The Field Guide draws every loop as a card. A small copy of the transit map, with the loop lit, sits on every card.

The whole system on one poster, and every loop on its own card.

The catalog page, as a page

The Charcoal head teaches R8 at full size with five numbered callouts, then plate A begins. At 1440 px first, then at 390 px.

The same card twice, at true size. Only the sign mark changes, and the reform foot is left off both.

The current system, the fallback

Concepts V2 stays the fallback if you choose none of the above (G1-11). Its R8 card and its loop catalog, at the same sizes as the pick's.

Report sections 4 to 7

Your decisions

Three choices

Choice 1 of 3

The systems maps

The studio's pick joins two directions. Loop Lines draws the whole system as a transit map on Prussian: each numbered loop is a line, each variable a station, and a variable shared by several loops is an interchange. It is the atlas's signature image and its 24 by 36 inch print. The Field Guide draws every loop as a smaller version of the R8 card you pointed to, on catalog pages of specimen plates. A small copy of the transit map, with the loop lit, sits on every card and catalog band, so a reader finds each loop on the poster.

Options: the pick (recommended); Loop Lines throughout; the Field Guide throughout; the current system, which stays the fallback (G1-11).

The cost: a reader meets two drawings, boxes on the cards and lines on the map. Shared names, shared line textures and the locator hold them together. The poster draws the 20 numbered loops, 25 variables and 46 connections; a note in its frame says so and points to the register for all 51 variables and 118 connections.

Studio recommendation The pick. See the maps above.

Choice 2 of 3

The icon concept

Overprint draws each icon as a fine Charcoal line over one solid plane of Pillar Red, set slightly off register toward the lower left, the way a second ink lands on a newspaper page. The red sits under the part of the subject the story is about: the opening of the door, the top stage, the gap where two halves meet. It answers your words, "premium simple line" with "a bit of pillar red in each one", and every rater who compared the families chose it. From 24 px up it is line with red; at 16 px it switches to a solid, one-color cut.

Options: Overprint (recommended); Moving part, solid pieces where the red piece is the one that moves, which holds up better at 16 px. Public sign stopped.

The cost: three drawings are still open and get done first in the build-out, the 16 px cut, Ballot and Campaign money (read as a printer and a camera in both concepts), and Testify. Two marks still fail the designer's look-alike checks: Bill's 16 px page against a bell, and Ballot against a printer.

Studio recommendation Overprint. See the icons above.

Choice 3 of 3

One sign mark everywhere

A step's sign (+ when the two variables move the same way, − when they move opposite ways) needs one mark across the cards, the catalog and the poster. The circled sign comes from Concept 08. The pointing tag, from Loop Lines, carries the sign and the direction the step runs. The review page shows the R8 card both ways at true size. Recommended: the pointing tag, a new mark beside M1 to M4.

Studio recommendation The pointing tag, a new mark beside M1 to M4. See the two R8 cards above.

Three calls that need your approval by name

Each changes approved geometry or the wording of Rule 05.3.

P1

The pillar marks' drawing

What changes
The four pillar marks keep their approved shapes and change how they are drawn: Overprint's fine line with its red plane from 24 px up, and a solid, one-color drawing at 16 px. This reverses the roles Gate 1 gave the solid and the line (Y1, Y4)
Why
Every rater who compared the families chose the line as more finished, and a line this fine breaks apart at 16 px, where solid shapes hold
P2

Act's lintel, at 16 px only

What changes
In the 16 px drawing, Act gains a lintel, a bar across the top of the doorway. The larger drawing keeps its frame and floor line
Why
Without it the small solid door reads close to the number 01, at the studio's 0.60 limit; with it the score falls to 0.23
P3

Rule 05.3, the current icon in a menu

What changes
The sentence "In a row or a menu, icons go one color and only the current one keeps its red." gains ", and that red counts as signature red."
Why
Without it, a menu's current icon spends the view's one working red, so a page could not show a menu and an ask button together

A question for you

Q-13, the reader check. Can five people who have never seen the brand look at the R8 card, the R10 card, the poster and the chosen icons, ten seconds each, and answer four questions: does the loop come back to the start, does it feed itself or push back, which step is least certain, and where does a reform act? The studio recommends running it before Gate 2. Every test so far used one agent rater and no people.

Report section 8

Risks

  • The poster leaves out the 26 variables and 72 connections that sit on no numbered loop. The note in its frame keeps that honest, and it must never leave the print.
  • Two drawing styles carry the maps. Readers may expect the cards to look like the poster; the reader check will show it.
  • The catalog scores 3 on beauty. A further pass on the catalog alone can follow your choice.
  • The station table and the district table need review whenever V7.1 changes a loop. The verifiers fail on any mismatch, so the risk is time.
  • Every icon reader so far is an AI agent. No person has named an icon (Q-13).
  • Atlas legends and tracker rows run at 16 px, and that cut is the least finished part of the icon family. At 16 px the family loses its line and its red, and looks like any careful solid set.
  • P1 means two drawings of every icon, about 60 icons with three masters each.
  • Overprint's distinctiveness rests on the fixed offset and on the red filling a drawn shape. Offset-accent sets are common in stock libraries, your own reference among them, so both rules have to hold across the whole set.
  • Signature reds stack: a social card can show the wordmark's ampersand, an icon's plane and the button's working red in one view. Rule 05.3 allows it, and it is more red than Phase 1 showed.

Report section 9

What happens after your answers

  1. The studio records your decisions and builds out the full icon set in the concept you choose, about 80 icons, with the same checks and a name test on every subject.
  2. The maps move into the guide as specs and working specimens in 15 Systems graphics (Phase 3) and 21 The atlas (Phase 4), per G1-08.
  3. Phase 2 continues with the identity, color, type, tokens and component chapters, and ends at Gate 2.
